ru: За́втра ты ни за что не угада́ешь отве́т.

Perfective side of the 'will succeed' collision is the correct half — a single completed outcome; the imperfective partner is retranslated instead.

Frame-only collision with the imperfective 'Don't be surprised'; the rest of the sentence ('to see me' vs 'it's normal') still cues which verb, and any reworking would misstate the gerund.

en: Knowing the truth, I would be less surprised.
note: 'marvel less' misreads удивля́ться here (being surprised, not admiring), and the gerund «Зна́я» can be kept as an English participle instead of being rebuilt as an if-clause.
'marvelled at' is the right sense of удивля́ться + dative here.
Compound imperfective future already reads as 'will be marvelling' — correct.
Imperfective negative imperative is the unmarked one; this half of the collision is correct.

en: He leaves the city every Friday.
note: 'by transport' is the headword gloss leaking into the sentence — no English speaker says it, and the verb's other examples all say just 'leave'.

ru: Они́ уезжа́ли ка́ждое ле́то на мо́ре.

note: Compound future correctly rendered 'will be leaving'.

en: I would not be leaving so early.
note: Fixes the 'would leave' collision on the imperfective side: the perfective partner «Будь де́ньги, я уе́хал бы на мо́ре» has a non-past protasis, so its present counterfactual is right and this half should carry the progressive.

ru: Будь де́ньги, я уе́хал бы на мо́ре.
note: «Будь де́ньги» is a non-past protasis, so the present counterfactual is correct; the collision is fixed on the imperfective side.

ru: Я уе́ду в дере́вню на неде́лю.

ru: Без газе́т я не узнава́л бы но́вости.
note: Progressive correctly distinguishes this from the perfective partner.

note: Protasis is бы+past, which is itself tense-ambiguous, and no collision forces the past-counterfactual reading, so the present reading stands.

en: I would have left if it had got boring.
note: Perfective with a past protasis («ста́ло») colliding with уходи́ть's 'would leave'; the past counterfactual forces уйти́ and leaves the imperfective as the only 'would leave'.

ru: Я уйду́ за́втра пора́ньше с рабо́ты.
note: Perfective single future is correct here; the wrong half of this 'will leave' collision is уходи́ть's compound future «бу́ду уходи́ть» ('will be leaving'), which is outside this packet.

note: Perfective single future is correct; the 'will indicate' collision is fixed on the imperfective partner, whose compound future was flattened.
«Стре́лка» glossed 'marksman' is a dictionary hole, not a translation defect.

en: The signs will be indicating the way to the sea.

ru: Она́ боя́лась, что у неё укра́ли су́мку.

note: «чужо́е» has no one-word English equivalent; 'what belongs to others' is the standard rendering.

en: Put the baby to bed as soon as possible.
note: A bare comparative 'sooner' has nothing to compare with in an English imperative; «поскоре́е» is 'as soon as possible'.

ru: За́втра ве́чером я уложу́ дете́й ра́ньше.

note: Imperfective habitual 'would smile more often' is correct; the 'would smile' collision is fixed on the perfective partner, which has a past protasis.
Frame-only collision against a perfective imperative — a statement versus a command is a clear cue, and both halves are correct as they stand.
Compound future correctly rendered 'will be smiling'.

ru: Е́сли б не уста́л, я улыбну́лся бы.
en: I would have smiled if I had not been tired.
note: Perfective single smile with a past protasis («не уста́л»), colliding with the imperfective's habitual 'would smile more often'; the past counterfactual forces улыбну́ться.

note: This is issue #576: the present counterfactual is what the imperfective слы́шать says, so the perfective must read as a single completed hearing, leaving 'would hear' to the partner.
Same frame collision as above; the perfective 'will hear' is correct and 'will be hearing' is not available for the imperfective side.
Simple past is correct for the perfective; the imperfective partner's 'We heard loud music' is also the natural English, so neither side is wrong.
Same as above — 'heard' is the only natural rendering on both sides of this pair.
